title: What does XLS-30 specify for AMM?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-30 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-30 specifies the XRPL automated market maker with liquidity-provider tokens, fee voting and an auction slot. [1]

A pool holds a pair of assets and issues LP tokens representing participation. Deposits and withdrawals change that participation; an auction bid can purchase a discounted trading-fee opportunity. These mechanisms do not promise a fixed yield or guarantee liquidity at a chosen price. Issuer token controls and enabled fixes remain relevant when assessing a particular pool. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-30 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-30 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
